## Library import
```{r}
library("ShortRead")
library("Rfastp")
library("ggplot2")
library("Rsubread")
```

## FastQ files
The first step needed is the QC and trimming of the FastQ files
under this is the example of how to do this on one file.

```{r}
se_json_report <- rfastp(read1 = file.path(getwd(),"FastQ","SRR3095866PE_1.fastq"), read2=file.path(getwd(),"FastQ","SRR3095866PE_2.fastq"),  outputFastq = paste0(file.path(getwd(),"FastQ","SRR3095866PE"),"postQC"), thread=4)

dfsummary <- qcSummary(se_json_report)
p1 <- curvePlot(se_json_report)

p1
```

## BAM files

First the BAM files need to be created for this 2 steps are needed to be run on a linux terminal using HISAT2.
First the reference genome has to be created using the amel_HVA_3.1 ->
# Extract splice sites and exons
hisat2_extract_splice_sites.py GCF_003254395.2_Amel_HAv3.1_genomic.gtf > splicesites.txt
hisat2_extract_exons.py GCF_003254395.2_Amel_HAv3.1_genomic.gtf > exons.txt

# Build index with annotation guides
hisat2-build -p 8 \
  --ss splicesites.txt \
  --exon exons.txt \
  GCF_003254395.2_Amel_HAv3.1_genomic.fna \
  Amel_HAv3.1_index

Using the reference genome we can perform gene alignment and mapping, HISAT2 handles this in one step
#gene alignment and mapping
hisat2 -p 8 \
  -x Amel_HAv3.1_index \
  -1 sample_R1.trim.fastq.gz \
  -2 sample_R2.trim.fastq.gz \
  --dta \
  --summary-file sample.align_summary.txt \
  | samtools sort -@ 4 -o sample.sorted.bam -

After creation of the bam files we need to do some checks to see the quality of the mapping and alignment

```{r}
bam_dir <- file.path(getwd(),"bam_files")
bam_files <- list.files(bam_dir, pattern = "\\.sorted\\.bam$", full.names = TRUE)

# Sanity check — make sure order and names are what you expect
bam_files

fc <- featureCounts(files = bam_files, annot.ext = file.path(getwd(),"ncbi_dataset/data/GCF_003254395.2/genomic.gtf"), isPairedEnd = TRUE, isGTFAnnotationFile = TRUE,
                    GTF.featureType = "exon",
                    GTF.attrType = "gene_id")


#take the perfomance stats from the bam files
stat_pct <- sweep(fc$stat[,-1], 2, colSums(fc$stat[,-1]), "/") * 100
rownames(stat_pct) <- fc$stat$Status
bam_qc_df_rnd <- data.frame(t(round(stat_pct, 1)))

#Create the sample names
bam_qc_df_rnd$samples <- gsub("\\.sorted\\.bam$", "", basename(colnames(counts)))


ggplot(bam_qc_df_rnd, aes(x=samples, y=Assigned)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",  fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1)
```

## Create count matrix
save the count information for further processing
```{r}
# The actual count matrix: genes x samples
counts <- fc$counts

# Clean up column names (they'll be full BAM paths by default)
colnames(counts) <- gsub("\\.sorted\\.bam$", "", basename(colnames(counts)))

head(counts)
dim(counts)   # genes x samples — sanity check
```
